classification.difficultyReason: Extract rectangle dimensions and kite diagonals from the coordinates, equate their areas using the proved formula, and justify cancellation from non-degenerate geometry.

content.prompt: The diagram shows a rectangle subtended by points $P(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta)$ and $P'(-r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta)$ on a semi-circle of radius $r$ with the $x$-axis.

spec.description: Upper semicircle, symmetric inscribed rectangle, coordinate axes and marked points O, T, P and P′. No angle marker or kite edges.
spec.mathematics: The rectangle has width 2r cos θ and height r sin θ. Diagram coordinates are illustrative; θ is not numerically specified.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry and labels are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the area of the rectangle is $r^2\sin2\theta$.

answer.short: The base is $2r\cos\theta$ and the height is $r\sin\theta$, so $A=2r^2\sin\theta\cos\theta=r^2\sin2\theta$.
answer.worked:
The base is $2r\cos\theta$ and the height is $r\sin\theta$.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{rectangle}}&=(2r\cos\theta)(r\sin\theta)\\A_{\text{rectangle}}&=2r^2\sin\theta\cos\theta\\A_{\text{rectangle}}&=r^2\sin2\theta.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The area of the rectangle is equal to the area of the kite $OPTP'$. Find the value of $\theta$.

inlines.text: Equate the rectangle area to half the product of the kite’s diagonals.

answer.worked:
The kite has perpendicular diagonals $OT=r$ and $PP'=2r\cos\theta$.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{kite}}&=\frac12(r)(2r\cos\theta)\\A_{\text{kite}}&=r^2\cos\theta.\end{align*}$$

Equate the areas and use the sine double-angle identity.

$$\begin{align*}r^2\sin2\theta&=r^2\cos\theta\\2r^2\sin\theta\cos\theta&=r^2\cos\theta\\2\sin\theta\cos\theta&=\cos\theta\\2\sin\theta&=1\\\sin\theta&=\frac12\\\theta&=30^\circ.\end{align*}$$

The non-degenerate rectangle has $0^\circ<\theta<90^\circ$, so $\cos\theta>0$ and division by $\cos\theta$ is valid.
